children: on Wednesday trimmed the top end of its annual production forecast after lowering expected volumes from its Beaumont New Ammonia plant in Texas, while stronger oil and gas prices helped third-quarter revenue beat estimates.
The country's top independent oil and gas producer now expects annual production of 174 to 181 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe), down from its earlier forecast of 174 to 185 mmboe.
Shares of the firm fell over 1% in early trading.

Woodside said lower expected volumes from Beaumont New Ammonia, tighter timeline for first LNG from the Scarborough project and reduced production at the Okha floating production, storage and offloading vessel weighed on its outlook.

The firm said production at its Beaumont New Ammonia facility was constrained to 69% of nameplate capacity during the quarter due to third-party feedstock availability and a roughly 30-day shutdown following a process safety event.
It also said it would begin a formal process to reduce its investment in Beaumont New Ammonia following a strategic review of the project.
The oil and gas producer reported revenue of $4.28 billion for the three months ended September 30, up from $3.36 billion reported a year ago, beating a Visible Alpha consensus of $4.11 billion.
Woodside's average realised price for its products rose 40% from a year earlier to $84 per barrel of oil equivalent, supported by stronger gas hub prices and the impact of LNG portfolio optimisation.

Quarterly production volumes fell 9% from a year earlier to 46.2 mmboe, but rose 12% from the previous quarter following higher production from Pluto LNG after maintenance activities were completed in the second quarter.
The company had earlier narrowed its annual production forecast in July, citing strong operational performance.
It also maintained its 2026 capital expenditure outlook at $4 billion to $4.5 billion.
